groups.h: Sampling distribution of the mean and the central limit theorem

dots.t: Define a statistical population as the entire group of people or objects about which information is sought
Define a sample as a selection of people or objects drawn from a population
Recognise that a statistic taken from a sample will be a good approximation if the sample is random and the sample size is large enough, typically n≥30
dots.m: Recognise that a statistic taken from a sample will be a good approximation if the sample is random and the sample size is large enough, typically <math><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></math>

dots.t: Recognise that, in general, the distribution of a population and a statistic, such as its mean, are unknown
Recognise that it is likely that the distribution of a random sample will resemble the distribution of the population when the sample size, n, is large enough, typically n≥30
dots.m: Recognise that it is likely that the distribution of a random sample will resemble the distribution of the population when the sample size, <math><mi>n</mi></math>, is large enough, typically <math><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></math>

dots.t: Define the sample mean for a sample X_1,X_2,…,X_n taken from a population as X‾=(1)/(n)∑_(i=1)^n X_i
dots.m: Define the sample mean for a sample <math><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mspace width="0.25em"/></mrow></math>taken from a population as <math><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>‾</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mrow><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></math>

dots.t: Recognise that the sample means obtained from repeated sampling may be different, even if all the samples are of the same size
Define, for a given sample size n, the sampling distribution of the mean to be the distribution of the sample means of all samples of size n
dots.m: Define, for a given sample size <math><mi>n</mi></math>, the sampling distribution of the mean to be the distribution of the sample means of all samples of size <math><mi>n</mi></math>

dots.t: Recognise that sample mean, X‾, is a random variable that estimates the population mean, μ, when the size of the sample is large enough and consider its usefulness in making predictions in a variety of contexts including politics, finance, agriculture and biology
dots.m: Recognise that sample mean, <math><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>‾</mo></mover></math>, is a random variable that estimates the population mean, <math><mi>μ</mi></math>, when the size of the sample is large enough and consider its usefulness in making predictions in a variety of contexts including politics, finance, agriculture and biology

dots.t: State the central limit theorem as: for a population with mean μ and variance σ^2, provided the sample size n is large enough (n≥30), the sampling distribution is approximately normal with mean μ and variance (σ^2)/(n); that is, X‾ is approximately N(μ,(σ^2)/(n))
dots.m: State the central limit theorem as: for a population with mean <math><mi>μ</mi></math> and variance <math><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, provided the sample size <math><mi>n</mi></math> is large enough (<math><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></math>), the sampling distribution is approximately normal with mean <math><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mspace width="0.25em"/></mrow></math>and variance <math><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>n</mi></mfrac></math>; that is, <math><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>‾</mo></mover></math> is approximately<math><mrow><mspace width="0.25em"/><mi>N</mi><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

dots.t: Recognise the significance of the central limit theorem for populations that are not necessarily normally distributed; that, irrespective of the population distribution, for a sufficiently large sample size, the sampling distribution of the mean is approximately normal
Use the formulas E(X‾)=μ and Var(X‾)=(σ^2)/(n) as the mean and the variance of the sampling distribution of the mean for samples of size n drawn from a population with mean μ and variance σ^2
